_comment: Archive gaps and season-level caveats. Every year from firstYear to the latest year in the workbook gets a Season row; years absent from Season History take their status from `gaps`. `overrides` adjust seasons that do exist in the workbook.

gaps.note: Newspaper coverage only. No scoresheets or secretary's letters survive for these years.
No documents survive. Longue Vue replaced Allegheny at some point in this stretch.

2011.statusNote: The file held only the secretary's letter and recap, no scoresheets, so 2011 has team totals only.

2022.statusNote: No Friday singles sheet survives. Totals cover Saturday and Sunday only and no final placings are given.

1949.statusNote: Allegheny's round totals sum to 65½ against a recorded final of 65. Unresolved; the error is on the original sheet.

1997.statusNote: Session totals sum to 577 against a recorded 576. Unresolved; the error is on the original sheet. Sunday itself balances.

1945.statusNote: Match 3 at Oakmont totals 73 where 72 points were played; the final standings carry the extra half point. Error on the original sheet.

1947.statusNote: Matches 2 and 3 total 180 points each, 36 more than eight-man teams can score; ten a side would give exactly 180. Whether the teams were larger that year or the sheet is wrong is unresolved.

2002.statusNote: The four finals total 575½ of 576 points played. Half a point is unaccounted for; player rows for 2002 are still to be transcribed.

2007.statusNote: The Sunday singles sheet credits 147 points where 144 were played; the recorded finals carry the extra 3. Error on the original sheet.

2023.statusNote: The Sunday singles sheet is a half point short between the Field Club and Fox Chapel; the recorded finals carry it. Error on the original sheet.

champions._comment: Who was engraved when first place was shared or contested. Keyed by year -> list of club ids. Years not listed: every club with place 1 is a champion (the 1999 no-playoff rule).

1953.note: Ended 168½-168½. Oakmont waived the trophy rather than play off, so the Field Club took its first title.
